summary: Crypto is easy to buy. Working out what you actually own, and who controls it, is the hard part. Manhar Garegrat of Liminal Custody takes the whole thing from first principles: why Bitcoin was built at all, how digital money can exist without a bank behind it, what blockchain, cryptography, mining and consensus actually do, and the question most buyers never ask, which is who holds the private keys when you buy through an exchange.

seo.description: Bitcoin, Ethereum and stablecoins from first principles: blockchain, mining, private keys, custody, Indian tax and the risks that matter.

takeaways.text: Buying crypto and owning crypto are not the same thing. If an exchange holds the private keys, the exchange holds the asset.
Bitcoin's 21 million limit, its halving schedule and its anonymous creator are not trivia. They are the design decisions that make the supply credible.
Mining, nodes and consensus are how a network with no central authority agrees on who owns what, and understanding that is the difference between investing and guessing.
An exchange, a broker and a custodian are three different roles. Knowing which one is holding your assets tells you what happens if it fails.
Indian crypto gains carry TDS and their own tax treatment, and losses cannot be set off the way they can elsewhere. Price is not the only thing to model.
